title: Carbon distribution in multi-phase gamma-TiAl based alloys and its influence on mechanical properties and phase formation

nodes.label: gamma-TiAl turbine alloys need more strength and creep resistance at temperature
Where carbon sits among gamma, alpha2 and beta-o, and what that does, has not been measured
Resolving the carbon distribution phase by phase should explain both the hardness changes and the phase selection
TNM as the reference beta-solidifying gamma-TiAl alloy
Add 0.75 at.% carbon as an interstitial solute (TNM0.75C)
Site-specific atom probe tips across phases and phase interfaces, plus nanoindentation of individual phase grains

attrs.reason: only these resolve composition and hardness phase by phase

nodes.label: Two alloys, C-free and C-bearing, compared in the same forged and homogenised condition
Melt and cast the ingots, TNM twice by VAR and TNM0.75C once by VIM
HIP at 1200 C, 200 MPa for 4 h, then hot forging and a homogenisation heat treatment
TNM is predominantly globular; TNM0.75C carries coarse lamellar colonies alongside globular grains
Carbon cuts the beta-o fraction from 19% to 2% and raises alpha2 from 11% to 37%
Carbon partitions strongly: about 1.2 at.% in alpha2, 0.3 at.% in gamma and almost none in beta-o
Carbon segregates at gamma/beta-o interfaces, more than doubling its gamma-side level there
Fine omega-o precipitates fill the beta-o of TNM and are absent from the beta-o of TNM0.75C
Interstitial carbon in gamma and alpha2 strains the lattice and impedes dislocation glide, hardening both phases
Carbon raises gamma hardness from 7.5 to 8.5 GPa and alpha2 hardness from 8.7 to 9.9 GPa
Carbon instead softens the beta-o phase, from about 10.0 to 8.9 GPa
The beta-o softening is the loss of omega-o precipitation hardening, not a solute effect, since Mo is higher in that beta-o
Shrinking the beta-o fraction concentrates Mo in it, and omega-o cannot nucleate because it must reject Mo into that matrix
Carbon-bearing TNM has higher strength and creep resistance at service temperature
Where the carbon goes sets both the hardening of gamma and alpha2 and the suppression of omega-o in beta-o
Literature hardness: pure beta-o is 8.0 GPa while beta-o + omega-o mixtures run 9.6 to 11.3 GPa
Solid-solution hardening scales as the square root of the solute concentration
Orientation relationship <111>beta-o {110}beta-o parallel to [0001]omega-o {11-20}omega-o
The rule-of-mixtures carbon balance gives 0.63 at.% against 0.78 measured, so 0.15 at.% is unaccounted for
Mo is about 2 at.% richer in the beta-o of TNM0.75C because so little of that phase remains

attrs.source: APT Table 3, not shown in the packet

nodes.label: The beta-o hardness itself reads as a presence test: 10.0 GPa matches a beta-o + omega-o mixture, 8.9 GPa matches pure beta-o
BSE: TNM is globular with a bright beta-o network along most boundaries; TNM0.75C mixes coarse lamellar colonies with globular grains and shows only isolated bright specks

attrs.image_note: both at a 30 um scale bar; in F1a the bright beta-o forms an interconnected network between the arrowed gamma and alpha2 grains, in F1b it survives only as a few isolated white specks. That near-disappearance is the clearest difference in the pair. Roughly half of the F1b field is still globular, so the C-bearing alloy is not 'largely lamellar'.

attrs.image_note: the interface in F2a is drawn as a 2.5 at.% Mo isosurface; only Mo (red) and C (blue) are plotted, so other solutes cannot be judged

notes: Lost: the boride phase, the XRD phase-fraction figure (MatMech records it as figure '?', and the packet carries no such figure), Tables 2-4 with the APT compositions and mean hardnesses, and the creep data behind the performance claim, which is argued rather than shown here. The diagnostic chain PRP/diagnostic -> KNW/lookup -> MEC/identification is the paper's own reasoning for omega-o presence. Audit: the gamma and alpha2 hardness histograms overlap heavily and their frequency axes carry no counts, so o4 is partial support for a 'substantial increase'. The SAD patterns in Figure 4 are unlisted insets, so o7 carries empty panel_ids.

changes: Added n14 -supports-> n18 and n26 -supports-> n18. n18 (MEC/identification) was a second spine root with no incoming spine edge; its only support ran through n28, which is off-spine. Both new edges are claims the node's own label rests on (omega-o absent in the C-bearing beta-o; Mo richer there).

o1 label corrected against the F1b crop: the C-bearing alloy is a mixture of lamellar colonies and globular grains, not 'largely lamellar'. The beta-o contrast reading, which is what carries n11, is unchanged.
o7 -> n14: moved the orientation_relationship aspect onto the edge, where v04 puts assign_features' op attribute.

panel_checks.note: F1a is the TNM BSE, globular, with beta-o, gamma and alpha2 arrowed and a bright interconnected beta-o network; F1b is TNM0.75C with lamellar colonies, globular grains and only a few isolated white specks. Both are the right panels and both show the beta-o contrast collapse the node reads. The 'largely lamellar' wording was too strong and has been corrected.

F3c is titled 'TNM beta-o phase' and F3f 'TNM0.75C beta-o phase'. F3c's mode is near 10 GPa with bars out past 11 GPa; F3f is narrow with a mode at ~8.9 GPa and nothing above ~9.7. The node's image_note is also right that only F3f carries the 8.0-12.0 GPa axis labels, so F3c has to be read against the shared axis.

F5c is the Mo proximity histogram with omega_o and beta_o labelled on either side of the interface: ~0.4 at.% on the omega-o side, a dashed c_max at ~4.7 at.% about 3 nm into beta-o, then a fall to ~3.0 at.%. Every value in the node label is on the panel.

review.audit_summary: Two audits (o4's overlapping hardness histograms with unlabelled frequency axes, and n25's 0.15 at.% carbon unaccounted for in the rule-of-mixtures balance), well under budget. Both are 'the figure/arithmetic does not fully resolve the claim', not contradictions, and both are stated that way: o4 carries image_support=partial into n16 rather than a qualifies edge to a weaker claim, and n25 is a DSC/limitation with kind=method. o7's empty panel_ids for the SAD insets is the honest treatment of an unlisted inset rather than an invented id.
